Summary Collaboration Themes: This collaboration integrated data science and ecological remote sensing to model tallgrass prairie vegetation phenology. Using MODIS-derived EVI and LSWI with Oklahoma Mesonet weather data, the team benchmarked linear, ensemble, and deep learning algorithms, including XGBoost, random forests, and neural networks. Their joint pipeline used time-series splits, grid-search tuning, and unseen 2022-2023 validation to test temporal transferability. The results showed temperature and solar radiation strongly drive vegetation indices, while rainfall and soil moisture effects were delayed, and ensemble methods outperformed deep learning. This cross-discipline work produced interpretable tools for predicting green-up, senescence, forage production, and drought-related ecosystem health, supporting ranching, hay management, conservation, and climate adaptation in Great Plains grasslands.
